data.gender_notes: Nalakuber is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Nalakuber is a name of Lord Vishnu, meaning the Lord of the Nalas. The name Nalakuber carries the meaning “Lord of the Nalas” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nalakuber usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the nalas and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_sanskrit.name: नलकूबर
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: Nala was a king who was exiled and cursed to become a serpent. He became the king of the Naga serpents and was known as Nalakuber.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Nalakuber" holds significant importance in Hindu mythology, reflecting the devotion and reverence for Lord Vishnu as the protector of the Nalas. The Nalas are a group of prominent disciples or followers of Lord Vishnu in Hindu texts. This cultural impact highlights the cherished belief in ancient Hindu scriptures, where the Lord is considered an intensely personal and loving deity, who blesses and protects his devotees.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, invoking the name "Nalakuber" speaks to the deep faith and surrender one has towards Lord Vishnu, seeking his blessings, protection, and guidance in their journey through life. It is believed that chanting the name brings peace, tranquility, and an inherent sense of divine connection, reminding one of the ultimate truth of the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nalakuber signifies the triumph of knowledge and devotion over the illusions of material desires. The name is derived from 'Nala' meaning knowledge and 'Kubera' symbolizing wealth and material pleasures, suggesting the victory of wisdom over worldly possessions.
